messages:
leo: hey folks — first day here. trying to get my Buildkite pipeline to publish an image to ghcr.io but the push fails with `denied: insufficient_scope: The token does not have the required scope.` i'm using a token supplied by the GitHub App integration. what perms am i missing?
priya: welcome! :wave: that message usually means the token lacks `packages:write`. GitHub App installation tokens often don't include package write scopes for GHCR pushes. which auth are you using in the pipeline?
leo: the pipeline has a secret called `GITHUB_APP_TOKEN` that we got from the Buildkite GitHub App. publish step does: 
```
docker login ghcr.io -u _json_key --password-stdin
docker push ghcr.io/redwood-inference/onboarding-demo:${BUILDKITE_BUILD_NUMBER}
```
and the login seems to accept the token but push fails with the insufficient_scope error.
tom: GitHub App tokens are good for many API operations but not for pushing container packages. For GHCR you need a PAT with `packages:write` or better a machine user PAT. Also: if the org enforces SSO, personal PATs can be blocked unless the user authorizes SSO.
leo: i tried to view the Buildkite app install but GitHub shows "Requires organization owner approval" and i get 403 on the org installs page. i don't have org-level perms.
priya: right — org owners must approve app installations. usually ops or a repo admin installs Buildkite at org level. meanwhile we create a repo-scoped machine user PAT as a workaround so CI can push without tying to your personal account. can you share the repo name here?
leo: repo is `onboarding-demo`. also FYI the pipeline secret i created was `GITHUB_TOKEN` (i may have assumed Actions auto-token). is that a problem?
tom: yes, `GITHUB_TOKEN` (the auto-provided Actions token) cannot be used for pushing to GHCR from external runners and has limited scopes. We expect `GHCR_PAT` or similar for Buildkite.
github-app-bot: Buildkite GitHub App status: not installed on repo onboarding-demo (installation requires approval).
priya: i'll spin up a machine user. we usually use `redwood-ci-bot` for pushes, grant Packages->Write on the repo, generate a PAT, and add it as a masked pipeline env `GHCR_PAT`. i'll also ask ops to approve the Buildkite app at org level so installs are smoother.
ci-bot: Buildkite build #7 failed 4 publish-image step (exit code 1).
tom: done: created machine user `redwood-ci-bot`, granted Packages:Write for onboarding-demo, generated PAT, added pipeline env `GHCR_PAT` (masked) to the onboarding pipeline, and approved Buildkite app for the repo.
ci-bot: Buildkite build #8 started (branch: onboard/leo-first-build).
leo: build #8  passed! thanks so much. quick questions: 1) where's the short doc that explains when to use `GITHUB_TOKEN` vs PAT vs machine user? 2) who do i ping to get apps approved for other repos?
priya: docs/dev/ci-auth.md covers that (short section). for app installs ping #eng-infra and tag @tom or @ops. we rotate machine user PATs quarterly; ops owns rotation but infra updates repo secrets as needed.
leo: awesome, appreciate the quick help — excited to be here :tada:
